name: Ulam
overview: Ulam was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh, identified specifically as the son of Peresh. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or significant narrative details provided beyond his lineage. As a descendant within the tribe of Manasseh, Ulam holds a place in the genealogical records of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Ulam means 'first' or 'leader,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. This meaning may suggest a position of prominence or importance, though the text does not explicitly state that the name was given by God. The name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:16.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ulam as the son of Peresh, as stated in 1 Chronicles 7:16. Additionally, it can be inferred that Bedan was his father, according to 1 Chronicles 7:17. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ulam's significance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical lineage of the tribe of Manasseh, serving as a link in the ancestral record preserved in 1 Chronicles. Though the biblical text provides limited information about him personally, his inclusion underscores the importance of tracing Israel's tribal heritage. His mention helps maintain the continuity of God's covenant people through successive generations.
